subject: Hosted API pricing follow-up — Marin Systems token profile & peak TPS
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@marinsys.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing follow-up — token volumes & peak TPS

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap + a couple of asks so we can get a draft pricing and canary plan over to you: 

1) Monthly consumption profile (high level): you said production starts in Q1 with a ramp —
   - Baseline: 40M tokens / month (customer service features, heuristics + assistant)
   - Expected steady-state: 120M tokens / month within 6 months
   - Peak month projection (marketing + feature launches): 220M tokens

2) Peak concurrency & TPS:
   - 99th percentile concurrent inference spikes: roughly 230 TPS sustained for short windows (1–5 minutes)
   - Sustained steady-state TPS during business hours: ~60 TPS

3) Budget & target $/1M tokens you mentioned: target range $28–$40 per 1M tokens depending on SLA/throughput guarantees and burst capacity.

Next steps from our side: we will produce two pricing scenarios by Friday — (A) conservative hosted price for self-serve with dynamic routing & autoscale, (B) committed-hosted slab with burst cap and discounting for 12-month commit. Both will show unit economics, estimated monthly cost, and a peak TPS allowance to match your SLA expectations. 

Action items for you: please confirm whether the peak TPS estimate (230 TPS) should be treated as a hard SLO load (we size for it) or as a bursty non-SLA event (we rely on fallback models/regions). Also, if you have a more detailed token composition (avg tokens per chat, embeddings volume), attach it to this thread.

I attached a short pricing worksheet and the notes we took during the demo — will annotate with model choices and expected per-token cost bands once you confirm the above.

Thanks — talk soon.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: marinsys-demo-notes.pdf (pdf)
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@marinsys.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing follow-up — token volumes & peak TPS

Thanks, Sergio — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

• Peaks: the 230 TPS is a hard peak we need to be able to support during product launches (we are running promotional campaigns with heavy bot traffic). We are open to a model where the committed plan guarantees a baseline 99th percentile of 200 TPS, and we accept a paid burst buffer for short windows above that.

• Token mix: our current average chat request is 1.8k tokens (including system + history), embeddings are relatively small right now (~2M vectors / month at 1536 dims), and latency requirement for chat is sub-500ms P99 ideally.

• Budget: target for committed pricing would ideally average $25–$32 / 1M tokens once we commit to a 12-month ramp. We can consider annual prepay to get to the low end.

I attached a short CSV export of current traffic samples (will send separately if the attachment bounces). Also, vendor compliance checks (SOC2) are on our procurement path, so we'll need a SOC2 attestation and a short data retention note.

Happy to take your scenarios and discuss next week.

—Alex
Director of Platform Engineering
Marin Systems
alex.chen@marinsys.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Oct 2025 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API pricing follow-up — next ops items & procurement path

Sergio / Karthik — quick internal note after Alex's reply: 

- Treat 200 TPS as the baseline SLO for committed pricing, with explicit burst billing above 200 up to 300 TPS (short windows). Legal will need to see exact wording for burst billing (per-minute or per-1k-token increments).
- Procurement asks: SOC2 attestation + short data retention & deletion note (we have a SOC2 package; I'll attach the standard compliance pack and a one-page retention summary).
- Pricing worksheet: I'll draft scenario A (self-serve/dynamic) and B (12-month commit + prepay) with the numbers Alex gave. Put conservative margin in case embeddings growth accelerates.

I'll loop in Solutions Engineering if we need a runbook for autoscaling thresholds and fallback models. Sergio — can you confirm whether we should propose per-minute burst increments or a per-request/1k-token unit? Alex seemed open to either but preferred per-minute so they can map to campaign windows.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
